name: M4 V66 A
description: The primary star of the eclipsing binary M4 V66, 0.7842 solar masses and 0.9347 solar radii; the two stars eclipse each other every 8.111 days.

radius.source: Primary radius (solar radii) 0.9347 +/- 0.0048, as DEBCat (Southworth 2015, ASPC 496, 164) lists it from Kaluzny et al. (2013AJ....145...43K)

mass.source: Primary mass (solar masses) 0.7842 +/- 0.0045, as DEBCat (Southworth 2015, ASPC 496, 164) lists it from Kaluzny et al. (2013AJ....145...43K)

temperature.source: Primary log Teff 3.79 +/- 0.007, as DEBCat (Southworth 2015, ASPC 496, 164) lists it from Kaluzny et al. (2013AJ....145...43K): 6166 K

gravity.source: Primary log g 4.388 +/- 0.077, as DEBCat (Southworth 2015, ASPC 496, 164) lists it from Kaluzny et al. (2013AJ....145...43K)

distance.source: Kaluzny et al. (2013), AJ 145, 43, the distance to M4 from V66 and V69: 1.82 +/- 0.04 kpc

text.card: The primary star of M4 V66, a pair that eclipse each other every 8.111 days.
text.introduction: It has 0.7842 solar masses and 0.9347 solar radii; its partner has 0.7443 and 0.8298, measured from the eclipses and the stars' motions.
text.locator: DEBCat (Southworth 2015, ASPC 496, 164), M4 V66: Mass, Radius and Period, from Kaluzny et al. (2013AJ....145...43K)

notes: Masses, radii and temperatures as DEBCat (Southworth 2015, ASPC 496, 164) (https://www.astro.keele.ac.uk/jkt/debcat/) lists them from Kaluzny et al. (2013AJ....145...43K).

SIMBAD knows it as [KTR2013] V66 (not Cl* NGC 6121 SAW V66, a different variable) and links no Gaia DR3 source; it is placed at Gaia DR3 6045465884181859712, 0.31 arcsec from the position in Kaluzny et al. (2013), Table 4, G = 16.47 against DEBCat's V = 16.84.

radialVelocity.source: No catalogued radial velocity: Gaia DR3 measures none for source 6045465884181859712 and SIMBAD lists none. Zero is assumed; a 30 km/s error moves the star by one part in 600,000 of its distance per century
